title: Staffing Coordinator: 14 RNs Short for Ride-Out

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Hospital Command Center Ext. 4520

callee.name: Dr. Marguerite Delacroix
callee.label: Chief Nursing Officer, Hospital Command Center

transcript.speaker: CNO
transcript.text: Command center, this is the CNO.

transcript.speaker: Staffing Coordinator
transcript.text: CNO, it's Rosalind Aguirre. Staffing. I need you for a minute. The House Supervisor needs to hear this too. The ride-out roster has 120 staff on paper, but I'm 14 RNs short.

transcript.speaker: Staffing Coordinator
transcript.text: Gulf Nurse Staffing has their 14 agency nurses staged in Portland. With contraflow running on US 181, it's outbound only, so they can't get across. I called their dispatcher at 361-555-0189 and the answer was, quote, maybe tomorrow, no promises.

transcript.speaker: Staffing Coordinator
transcript.text: ICU and NICU, Wednesday night. ICU is 4 short, so ICU goes to one to three instead of one to two. In the NICU I can keep one to one on the three vented babies, but the other nine go to one to three. NICU is 3 short. Med-surg absorbs the rest of the gap.

transcript.speaker: Staffing Coordinator
transcript.text: I haven't moved anyone yet. I don't want to pull from med-surg until I know how many discharges we're getting today. And the ride-out teams aren't due in until tomorrow evening under the timeline.

transcript.speaker: Staffing Coordinator
transcript.text: So tell me how you want this handled. Do I build Wednesday night at those ratios, or do we do something different? I need an answer before I lock the roster at 08:00.

voiceStyles.Staffing Coordinator: Experienced nurse in her 40s, organized but tense, talking fast, keyboard and phones ringing in a busy staffing office behind her
voiceStyles.CNO: Calm senior nursing executive, brief and focused, quiet command-center chatter in the background

instructorNote: This tests escalation. The ICU is more than 3 nurses short, so the CNO should escalate within 15 minutes and should not accept a 1:3 ICU ratio. Watch whether the CNO and House Supervisor work through redeployment, early discharges and calling ride-out staff in early, and whether the CNO tells the IC that ride-out staffing (106 of 120, below the 90% threshold) now bears on the shelter-or-evacuate decision.
